pluginManager.title: Plugins
pluginManager.lead: Switch plugins on and off. A plugin that is off disappears from the menu; the services behind it (e.g. WireGuard or the firewall) keep running.
pluginManager.empty: No plugin.json in the plugins/ folder.
pluginManager.sectionInactiveHint: Plugins that can be switched on right away come first, then those that need packages installed.

login.title: Sign in
login.codeHint: Enter the 6-digit code from your authenticator app or a backup code.

theme.title: Appearance
theme.hint: The choice applies immediately in this browser and is stored for the account.

overview.title: Overview
overview.sample: Part of the host data is a Debian sample value.
overview.doctorHint: Same check as sudo godeb-play doctor. Output without secrets.

panel.mocked: Sample data: the program or file this page needs is missing on this server.

app.unknownBody: No plugins/ folder with a valid manifest.json exists for {{id}}.
app.notReady: The folder exists, but the Go handler is not registered.
app.noView: The React view is still missing.
app.crashText: The rest of GoDeb keeps running. Please include the message below if it happens again.

fail2ban.title: Fail2ban
fail2ban.description: Addresses banned after too many failed attempts (sign-in, SSH, mail).
fail2ban.noneBlocked: No IP is blocked right now.

logs.title: Log
logs.description: Sign-ins, actions and errors of GoDeb.

monitor.title: Monitoring
monitor.description: Health of the server, history and events.
monitor.notChecked: The first check is still running.
monitor.noData: No samples in this time range yet.
monitor.noEvents: No events in this time range.

network.noAccounting: No counters yet. The agent creates the table inet godeb_acct on its first run (needs nftables).
network.noBytes: The kernel counts bytes per connection only with net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_acct=1, so the list shows counts only.

access.noBlocks: No blocks logged (ufw logging off or nothing blocked).
access.clamped: Access is read straight from the journal and goes back at most 7 days.

sites.none: No sites yet. "sudo godeb site add" on the hub or WireGuard → new peer → "Site" creates one.

alerts.intro: GoDeb sends a message for new problems and warnings, and optionally when they are resolved. The same finding is repeated at most every 6 hours unless it gets worse. On the hub, problems of the sites count too.
alerts.mailMissing: Mail is not set up yet: {{detail}}
alerts.ntfyHint: Install the ntfy app on the phone and subscribe to the same topic. The topic is the password: make it long and random.
alerts.note: Unusually high traffic or CPU load counts as a hint, ten times the usual value as a warning. GoDeb learns the usual values from the history (first values after three days).

apt.title: APT
apt.description: Package updates of this server. GoDeb looks for new packages regularly and can install security updates on its own.
apt.selfHint: This includes a GoDeb update. The interface restarts briefly; the update itself keeps running and shows up here afterwards.
apt.autoSecurityHint: Only packages from the Debian security sources (trixie-security), right after the check. Everything else, GoDeb included, stays with "Update all". A new kernel needs a reboot afterwards.
apt.restarting: No connection: GoDeb restarts after updating itself. The page reconnects in a moment.

certbot.title: Certbot
certbot.description: Let’s Encrypt certificates of this server and when they expire.
certbot.name: Name
certbot.subject: Subject

systemd.title: Services
systemd.overviewDescription: The important services of this server with status and usage.

confirm.stop: Really stop {{name}}? Access to the server (SSH, the tunnel to this interface) or its protection may depend on it.
confirm.restart: Restart {{name}}? The connection may drop briefly.

reboot.title: Server
reboot.required: Reboot needed for updates (usually the kernel) to take effect.
reboot.confirm: Reboot the server in one minute? All services, the tunnel and this interface will be gone for a few minutes. Until then the reboot can be cancelled.
reboot.autoBefore: Reboot at night when updates require it, at
reboot.autoHint: Only when /run/reboot-required exists and no APT run is active, with one minute's notice. Server local time, one-hour window. Give hub and home VM different times.

ufw.name: Firewall
ufw.description: Loads the ufw rules at boot

portforward.name: Port forwarding
portforward.description: Loads the NAT rules to sites

opendkim.name: OpenDKIM
opendkim.description: DKIM signing for the mail gateway

postgres.title: PostgreSQL
postgres.description: Databases and users. Reachable from this server only, never public.

websites.title: Websites
websites.description: Your own websites and proxies to internal services, with a Let’s Encrypt certificate.
websites.name: Name
websites.addHint: After creating, set DNS (A), then use Certificate for Let's Encrypt.

cron.title: Scheduled tasks
cron.description: Scheduled tasks of this server. New tasks run as systemd timers with approved commands only.
cron.addHint: No shell. Allowed: fixed binaries (true, logrotate, certbot renew, systemctl reload …; certbot without hooks, logrotate only with configs below /etc) or scripts in the allowlisted directories.
cron.name: Name
cron.cronDHint: Classic cron.d files are shown only, not edited.

remote.title: Temporary remote access
remote.hint: For the setup while the tunnel is not ready yet: the interface is then reachable by HTTPS at {{ip}}:{{port}} from anywhere.
remote.openUntil: Reachable from outside until {{until}}. Afterwards the access closes on its own.
remote.safety: HTTPS only with a self-signed certificate (browser warning). Sign-in with password and 2FA, fail2ban bans after failed attempts. With the Hetzner Cloud Firewall, allow port 8443/tcp there as well.

wg.title: WireGuard
wg.description: Tunnel and devices. New devices get a QR code or a file.
wg.name: Name
wg.excludedHint: These networks are subtracted from AllowedIPs (e.g. all traffic through the tunnel except your LAN).
wg.needConfig: Peers cannot be created without a readable wg0.conf.
wg.qrHint: Scan it in the WireGuard app.
wg.emailHint: The file contains a private key.
wg.androidDescription: GoDeb Tunnel APK with smart auto-disconnect on trusted networks.
wg.androidUnavailable: No APK on the server yet. Place a signed build at {{path}}.
wg.androidQrHint: After install: import the peer via QR or .conf, then enable auto-disconnect.
wg.androidTokenHint: Optional download token: without a token the download stays public (only sensible behind the tunnel). With a token the link needs ?token=…
wg.androidTokenOn: APK download now requires a token.
wg.androidTokenOff: APK download no longer requires a token.
wg.siteLabel: Site (GoDeb server behind this hub, e.g. the home VM)
wg.siteHint: Tunnel network only, no DNS, keepalive 25. Phone and laptop reach the site's web UI through this hub.
wg.deviceKeyHint: Paste only the public key. The private key stays on the device; GoDeb does not store a client file.
wg.deleteAfterDownloadHint: Removes the .conf with the private key from the server. The peer in wg0.conf stays.
wg.configDeleted: Client file for {{name}} deleted from the server.
wg.peerRoleText: This server is connected to hub {{hub}} with address {{address}}. Create new clients and sites on the hub.
wg.volltunnelText: Clients with AllowedIPs 0.0.0.0/0 send all their internet traffic through this hub (IP forwarding and NAT in a dedicated nftables table).
wg.volltunnelWarn: Uses VPS bandwidth and traffic. If the tunnel drops, those clients have no fallback. Sites (home VM) stay without a full tunnel.
wg.volltunnelConfirm: Enable full tunnel? Affected clients will send all internet traffic through this server.
wg.joinText: No wg0 yet. Paste the join code or client file the hub created for this site (wizard, "sudo godeb site add" or WireGuard → site → Code). Only keys, address, endpoint, AllowedIPs inside the tunnel network and keepalive are accepted.
wg.trustDescription: On the home Wi-Fi the GoDeb Tunnel app asks this server directly (outside the tunnel). It signs the request with its own key; only then the app switches the tunnel off. A foreign network cannot fake this.
wg.trustRunning: Active – answers requests from the home network.
wg.trustNotRunning: Enabled, but the listener is not running. {{error}}
wg.trustSynced: {{count}} client file(s) updated. Re-scan the QR code on the devices.
wg.trustHubHint: New clients get the trusted endpoints of this server and all sites in their configuration automatically. After changes on a site, “Update client files” and re-scan the QR code.
wg.trustPeerHint: The hub copies address and key into new phone configurations automatically. Existing ones: “Update client files” on the hub, then re-scan the QR code.

enroll.title: Set up two-factor authentication
enroll.intro: 2FA is mandatory for this account. You need an authenticator app.
enroll.scan: 1. Scan the QR code with the app
enroll.qrAlt: QR code for the authenticator app
enroll.manual: Cannot scan? Enter the key manually:
enroll.warning: Print or store them safely! Each code works exactly once.
enroll.sheetText: Each code replaces the code from the authenticator app exactly once, e.g. when the phone is lost. Tick off used codes.
enroll.sheetKeep: Keep safe and apart from the phone. New codes only come with a new 2FA setup.

mailgw.title: Mail gateway
mailgw.description: Postfix stores inbound and outbound mail and forwards it to the home server through the WireGuard tunnel.
mailgw.relayHint: Next hop {{host}}:25. While it is unreachable, mail stays in the queue.
mailgw.noDomain: No domain yet. The DNS check starts after setup.
mailgw.flushed: The queue was asked to deliver.

domains.title: Domains
domains.description: Register domains once. GoDeb shows the DNS records plugins need (e.g. mail), checks them live, and can publish them through the Hetzner Cloud API.
domains.hetznerHint: API token for a project that owns the DNS zones (read and write only). GoDeb only changes records labelled godeb=1 and creates new ones that way. Reverse DNS (PTR) uses the same token on the server.
domains.name: Domain
domains.domainLead: Records from plugins and live checks.
domains.deleteConfirm: Remove domain {{name}} from GoDeb? DNS records at the provider stay.
domains.needToken: Store a Hetzner API token above first.
domains.zoneMissing: The zone {{name}} does not exist in this token's Hetzner project. Create it in the Hetzner Console under DNS (and point the nameservers at your registrar to Hetzner) or store the token of the right project. Until then only manual mode works.
domains.recordsHint: Missing records show as “missing”. With Hetzner, “Apply at Hetzner” only writes GoDeb-owned (labelled) records; others stay untouched and are reported as conflicts.
domains.noRecords: No plugin supplies records for this domain. Set up the mail server with this domain first.
domains.noMailDomain: There is no mail domain for this domain yet.
domains.mailNotInstalled: The mail server is not set up yet.
domains.defaultsHint: Web (domain and www), mail, webmail, MX, SPF and DMARC point to this server. Records of the plugins (mail server, websites) take precedence.

mail.title: E-mail
mail.description: Mail server with domains, mailboxes, forwarding and spam filter.

setup.title: Set up the mail server
setup.text: GoDeb installs Postfix (SMTP), Dovecot (IMAP), Rspamd (spam filter, DKIM) and Redis and configures them securely. Then you add domains and mailboxes.
setup.hostnameHint: Full name, e.g. mail.example.com. It needs an A record pointing to {{ip}} and a matching reverse DNS (PTR) at the hosting provider.
setup.gateway: The mail gateway is set up on this server with {{count}} relay domain(s). Both configure Postfix; remove those domains first.
setup.what1: Ports 25 (incoming), 465 and 587 (sending with login only) and 993 (IMAP, encrypted only) are opened in the firewall.
setup.what2: Login only over TLS, senders only as their own address, Fail2ban bans after failed attempts, passwords only as Argon2id hash.
setup.what3: Until the Let's Encrypt certificate is issued the server uses a self-signed one.

mail.clamavHint: Scans every message for viruses. Needs about 1.5 GB more RAM; better off on a small VPS.
mail.certHint: Port 80 opens only briefly while the certificate is issued and renewed. The hostname must point to this server.
mail.hostNotResolved: {{host}} does not point to {{ip}}. Add the A record at your DNS provider, otherwise there is no certificate and other servers cannot find this one.

queue.title: Queue ({{count}})
queue.hint: Mail Postfix could not deliver yet. Retry or delete.
queue.mocked: Sample data – postqueue is not available here.

mail.addDomainHint: GoDeb creates a DKIM key and then shows you the DNS records.
mail.passwordHint: At least 10 characters. The suggestion is random; GoDeb stores only a hash.
mail.newPasswordHint: Leave empty to keep the password.
mail.quotaHint: 0 = unlimited. At 80% and 95% usage the mailbox receives a warning mail.
mail.aliasesHint: More addresses @{{domain}} for this mailbox, one per line. It may send from them too.
mail.forwardHint: Copy to these addresses, one per line.
mail.forwardOnlyHint: Mail goes only to the forwarding addresses, without a mailbox and without login.
mail.suspendHint: No login and no sending; incoming mail is still delivered.
mail.vacationHint: Automatic reply to senders (Sieve). At most once per sender within the chosen interval.
mail.vacationBodyPlaceholder: I am currently away and will reply when I return.
mail.vacationDaysHint: Minimum days between replies to the same sender (1–30).
mail.confirmDeleteAccount: Delete {{address}} with all its mail? This cannot be undone.
mail.credentialsOnce: The password is shown only now. GoDeb does not store it.
mail.dnsHint: Create these records at the domain's DNS provider. Changes often take a few minutes.

dnsHelp.mx: Tells other servers where mail for this domain goes.
dnsHelp.spf: Allows only this mail server to send for the domain.
dnsHelp.dkim: Public key receivers use to check this server's signature.
dnsHelp.dmarc: Receivers should treat mail failing SPF/DKIM as spam.
dnsHelp.mtasts: Points to the MTA-STS policy. id changes when the policy changes.
dnsHelp.tlsrpt: Where other servers send TLS failure reports (mailto). Create a mailbox or catch-all for tls-reports@.
dnsHelp.a: The mail server hostname must point to this IP (once for all domains).
dnsHelp.autoconfig: Thunderbird fetches IMAP/SMTP settings from here.
dnsHelp.autodiscover: Outlook fetches IMAP/SMTP settings from here.
dnsHelp.ptr: Set at the hosting provider (Hetzner: server → networking → reverse DNS). Without a matching PTR mail often lands in spam.

mail.mtaSTSPolicyHint: File for https://{{host}}/.well-known/mta-sts.txt (mode=testing until the web server serves it). Stored under /etc/godeb-play/mta-sts/.
mail.catchAllHint: Mail to unknown addresses of this domain goes here. Empty = reject (recommended, less spam).
mail.suspendDomainHint: No new mail accepted, no login. Mailboxes and data are kept.
mail.deleteDomainHint: Deletes {{domain}} with {{count}} mailboxes, all mail and the DKIM key. Type the domain name to confirm.

client.text: How to set up a mailbox in Thunderbird, Outlook or on a phone:
client.selfSigned: Still with a self-signed certificate: mail clients warn until the Let's Encrypt certificate is issued.

mail.postmasterCreated: Mailbox {{address}} created, plus the aliases {{aliases}} for abuse reports and the DMARC and TLS reports. Password:
mail.postmasterOnce: Shown only now. Write it down or set a new one on the mailbox later.
mail.roleTargetHint: postmaster@, abuse@, dmarc@ and tls-reports@ go to this existing address. Empty: a postmaster@ mailbox of its own.

ens.name: Server name
ens.customHint: Factors for the Custom preset. Other keys stay intact in the File view.
ens.noGroups: No groups: the server is open without a password.

stepUp.title: Confirm with 2FA
stepUp.window: This action changes the server. Enter a current code from your authenticator app. It then covers further actions for 5 minutes.
stepUp.critical: This action can change access to the server or install software. It needs your password and a new code every time.
stepUp.backupHint: Without your phone, a backup code works too. Each code works once: wait for the next code before the next action.
stepUp.remaining_one: {{count}} attempt left, then the session ends.
stepUp.remaining_other: {{count}} attempts left, then the session ends.

sessions.title: Sessions
sessions.hint: Every device you are signed in on. Ended sessions stop working immediately.

pf.title: Port forwarding
pf.description: Forward public ports of this server to a site, e.g. the game server on the home VM.
pf.name: Name
pf.rulesHint: Ports from 1024, at most 1000 per rule. SSH, WireGuard and the GoDeb UI cannot be forwarded. Every change needs a fresh 2FA code.
pf.snatHint: Replies return through the tunnel because the hub rewrites the source address to {{hub}}. The service on the site therefore sees every connection from {{hub}}; banning players by IP does not work there.

setup.title: First-run setup
setup.adminText: The first user manages this server. In the next step you set up two-factor sign-in.
setup.tokenHint: Part of the link from “sudo godeb-play setup-url” or in /etc/godeb-play/setup-token.
setup.roleText: GoDeb Play joins your GoDeb hub (VPS) as a site. Players then reach the game servers through the hub's public IP, without port forwarding on the home router.
setup.roleHubText: For a VPS with a public IP. Phones, laptops and sites connect here.
setup.rolePeerText: Recommended. On the hub, add a site under WireGuard (or "sudo godeb site add games") and paste the join code here.
setup.roleNoneText: Only for trying it on the home network. The game servers are not reachable from outside then.
setup.endpointHint: IP or host name clients use to reach this server.
setup.fullTunnelHint: Optional. Clients then send all traffic through the hub (NAT). Uses bandwidth; no fallback if the tunnel drops. Sites stay without a full tunnel.
setup.joinHint: Paste the join code from the hub (starts with godeb-join:) or upload the file. It is shown in the hub's wizard, under WireGuard → site → Code, or by "sudo godeb site add".
setup.qrHint: Scan with the GoDeb Tunnel app. The code contains the client's private key.
setup.joinNoHandshake: No handshake with the hub yet.
setup.accessText: How should the interface be reachable after setup? This setup page closes afterwards.
setup.accessTunnelText: Safest: only from the tunnel (http://10.8.0.x:8080). Recommended for a VPS.
setup.accessLanText: Also via HTTPS from your own LAN, allowed for that subnet only.
setup.trust: Offer the trusted endpoint in the home network
setup.trustHint: The GoDeb Tunnel app then switches the tunnel off on the home Wi-Fi.
setup.firewallActive: Add rules to the active firewall (ufw)
setup.firewallHint: SSH ({{ports}}/tcp) stays open, otherwise only what is needed. The setup port gets closed.
setup.firewallNoSsh: SSH port not detected, so ufw stays off.
setup.ufwMissing: ufw is not installed; please set up the firewall yourself.
setup.doneText: Setup is complete. You now reach the interface here:
setup.nextTunnel: Connect the tunnel, then open http://<tunnel address>:8080
setup.listenerClosed: This setup page is no longer reachable from now on.
setup.summaryHint: Everything at a glance. Best print it or save it as PDF now; later again under Overview → Setup overview or with "sudo godeb-play summary".
setup.joinPlaceholder:
godeb-join:…

or the content of the file:
[Interface]
PrivateKey = …
setup.servicesText: Optional: what a new server usually needs next. Everything can be changed later on the Domains, E-mail and Mail gateway pages.
setup.relayHostHint: Address of the home site in the WireGuard network, usually 10.8.0.2. Port 25 is opened in the firewall.
setup.domainsText: Enter all domains you own. GoDeb adds them under Domains and creates the DNS records for web, e-mail and webmail.
setup.dns_hetznerText: With an API token from the Hetzner Console, GoDeb creates the records itself and keeps them up to date. The zones must be in the same project.
setup.dns_manualText: GoDeb shows the records to copy and checks them live afterwards.
setup.tokenStored: A Hetzner token is already stored.
setup.hetznerTokenHint: Hetzner Console → project → Security → API tokens, read and write. Stored sealed in the agent.
setup.domainListHint: One per line or separated by commas, without www.
setup.defaultsHint: Domain and www, mail and webmail point to this server, plus MX, SPF and DMARC. With the mail relay or mail server, DKIM is added.
setup.domainManual: please enter at your DNS provider
setup.mailText: Where should e-mail for your domains arrive?
setup.mail_noneText: Set it up later under E-mail or Mail gateway.
setup.mail_relay: Mail relay to the home server
setup.mail_relayText: This server accepts mail and passes it through the tunnel to the mail server at home. If that is unreachable, mail waits up to 5 days.
setup.mail_serverText: Mailboxes, spam filter and DKIM right here (Postfix, Dovecot, Rspamd). Needs about 1 GB of RAM.
setup.mailHostnameHint: Name mail clients use to reach the server. GoDeb creates the A record; with a Hetzner token it also sets the reverse DNS.
setup.mailboxHint: Each domain gets the mailbox postmaster@ with the aliases abuse@, dmarc@ and tls-reports@. The reports the DNS records ask for arrive there.
setup.serverReady: The mail server is set up ({{host}}).
setup.serverInstalling: Installing the mail server, this takes a few minutes …
setup.domainsWorking: Creating domains, mailboxes and DNS records …
setup.mailboxOnce: Shown only now. Write it down or set a new one later under E-mail.
setup.certText: Mail clients expect a valid certificate for {{host}}. As soon as the A record is visible worldwide (at Hetzner usually within minutes), GoDeb gets it from Let's Encrypt.
setup.certStarted: Running in the background; the E-mail page shows the progress.
setup.firstMailbox: Create a first e-mail address of your own
setup.firstMailboxHint: Your mailbox, e.g. firstname@your-domain. You sign in with it in Thunderbird or on your phone.
setup.mailboxPasswordHint: 10 to 128 characters. Stored only as a hash.
setup.rolesToMailbox: Send postmaster@, abuse@, dmarc@ and tls-reports@ of all domains to {{address}}
setup.rolesToMailboxHint: Everything arrives in your mailbox, no postmaster mailbox of its own. Aliases in the same domain, forwards for the other domains.

clients.title: Devices and sites
clients.text: Every phone, laptop and GoDeb server at home gets its own access. Add as many as you need now. Later this is under WireGuard.
clients.kindDeviceText: QR code for the app, file for the laptop
clients.kindSiteText: E.g. the home VM. Gets a join code to paste.
clients.name: Name
clients.deviceHint: Phone: scan with the GoDeb Tunnel app. Laptop: download the file and import it into WireGuard. The access only reaches the tunnel network; other traffic stays outside.
clients.deviceHintFull: Phone: scan with the GoDeb Tunnel app. Laptop: download the file and import it into WireGuard. Full tunnel: all internet traffic goes through this server.
clients.siteHint: On the GoDeb server at home, choose "Connect to hub" in the wizard and paste this code. It then connects directly to this server.
clients.secret: Contains the private key of this access. Only paste or scan it where it belongs; do not pass it on by chat or mail.

summary.title: Setup of {{host}}
summary.noSecrets: This overview contains no passwords, tokens or private keys. The WireGuard client files are on the server in /etc/wireguard/clients.

tunnel.label: Through the WireGuard tunnel
tunnel.note: Connect the WireGuard tunnel, then open in the browser.

tunnelPeer.label: Through the WireGuard tunnel
tunnelPeer.note: Reachable through the hub's tunnel (phone or laptop connected to the hub).

lan.label: In the home network (HTTPS)
lan.note: Self-signed certificate: compare the fingerprint below.

upload.tooLarge: The file is too large for a WireGuard configuration.
upload.notWireGuard: This is not a WireGuard file ([Interface] and [Peer] are missing).

apphttps.title: App access
apphttps.description: GoDeb under its own name with a valid certificate inside the tunnel, so the interface can be installed as an app on a phone. It stays closed from outside.
apphttps.runningHint: Let's Encrypt is checking the DNS record. This usually takes one to three minutes.
apphttps.pendingHint: No certificate yet. Check the error above and choose “Get certificate again”.
apphttps.installHint: With the tunnel up, open this address in the browser, sign in and choose “Install app” or “Add to home screen” in the menu.
apphttps.setupHint: Creates a DNS record pointing to the tunnel address and gets a Let's Encrypt certificate through the Hetzner API.
apphttps.name: Name
apphttps.needTunnel: This server has no WireGuard tunnel (wg0).
apphttps.needToken: No Hetzner API token is stored under Domains.
apphttps.needZone: No domain in Hetzner mode is registered under Domains.
apphttps.detailPort: HTTPS listens only on the wg0 address, port {{port}}; ufw allows the port on wg0 only.
apphttps.detailDns: The A record publicly points to the private tunnel address. Without the tunnel nothing is reachable through it.
apphttps.detailRenew: The agent renews the certificate 30 days before it expires and reports errors in monitoring.
apphttps.detailSite: On a site (home VM) the hub currently forwards only port 8080 between peers, so the name is not yet reachable from the phone there.

steam.installHintSeeded: The server files are already present. Installing only validates them (SteamCMD validate), fetches what is missing and sets up Wine, config, service and firewall.
steam.confirmRestart: Really restart the server? Players will be disconnected.
steam.confirmUpdate: Start update? The server will be stopped, updated and started again.
steam.defaultShown: No file yet. Showing the template that is written on save or install.
steam.notObject: The file must be a JSON object.
steam.fixJsonFirst: Fix the JSON first, then switch to the simple view.
steam.saved: Saved. Takes effect on the next server start.
steam.behindHub: This server is a site of hub {{hub}}. Players connect to {{hub}}:{{port}}. For that, the hub needs a port forwarding in GoDeb for {{ports}}/udp to {{address}} (plugin “Port forwarding”, template Enshrouded). Here the ports are open inside the tunnel only.
steam.title: Game servers
steam.description: Install, update and configure game servers.
steam.installHint: Installs SteamCMD{{wine}}, downloads the server (about {{size}} GB), creates config and service and opens the UDP ports. Takes 5–20 minutes depending on the connection. The server needs about {{memory}} GB RAM.

backups.title: Savegames
backups.hint: {{dir}} is backed up before every update and on request; the last {{keep}} backups are kept. The server pauses briefly for a backup.
backups.confirmRestore: Restore the savegame from {{time}}? The server stops briefly; the current state is backed up first.
